rationale: C17 is a direct and highly specific drafting template. The child repeats its seven-recital structure, the same Annecy accession and Cuban-agreement background, the same two linked presidential determinations, and the same two-part operative machinery. It principally substitutes Sweden and April 30, 1950 for Greece and March 9, 1950, changes the identified concessions, and adapts the Cuban-list amendment from deleting one item to revising and deleting several items. The child also expressly identifies C17 as a supplement to the December 22, 1949 proclamation. C03 and C16 are strong earlier ancestors of the same two-track GATT/Cuba supplement structure, but their language and machinery are less immediately congruent than C17's.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the trade agreement for accession ... has been signed by the Government of the Kingdom of Sweden ... and such Government will become a contracting party ... on April 30, 1950
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the trade agreement for accession ... has been signed by the Government of the Kingdom of Greece ... and such Government will become a contracting party ... on March 9, 1950
shared_material.explanation: The child closely reuses the accession-trigger recital, changing only the acceding government and effective date.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas I determine that the application of each of the concessions provided for in Part I of Schedule XX in Annex A ... which were withheld from application ... is required or appropriate to carry out, on April 30, 1950, the said trade agreement for accession
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas I determine that the application of each of the concessions provided for in Part I of Schedule XX in Annex A ... which were withheld from application ... is required or appropriate to carry out, on and after March 9, 1950, the said trade agreement for accession
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive shared language implementing the same withheld-concession machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas I determine that, in view of the determination set forth in the sixth recital ... [specified revisions and deletion] are required or appropriate to carry out ... the said exclusive trade agreement
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas I determine that, in view of the determination set forth in the sixth recital ... the deletion of Item 328 ... is required or appropriate to carry out ... the said exclusive trade agreement
shared_material.explanation: Both use the general-agreement concession determination to trigger a corresponding amendment to the Cuban tariff list.

shared_material.child_excerpt: PART I ... the identification of each of the concessions ... included in the sixth recital ... shall ... be included in the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of December 22, 1949
shared_material.parent_excerpt: PART I ... the identification of each of the concessions ... included in the sixth recital ... shall ... be included in the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of December 22, 1949
shared_material.explanation: The core operative sentence is nearly verbatim, with only the effective date and referenced supplemental list adapted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: PART II ... the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948 ... shall ... be further amended by revising ... deleting ... and ... revising
shared_material.parent_excerpt: PART II ... the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948 ... shall ... be further amended by deleting therefrom the Item 328
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves the same second-part administrative machinery while substituting a more complex set of item-level amendments.
